description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts, fix a regex in surqlBreakingFieldRefusal that lets a hazardous migration through.

Replace this exact line, which is indented with SIX spaces and occurs once:

      if (/\b(DEFAULT|VALUE)\b/i.test(rest)) continue; // has a value => safe

with a version whose keyword match cannot be satisfied by a variable name, keeping the same indentation, the same `continue`, and an updated trailing comment:

      if (/(?<!\$)\b(DEFAULT|VALUE)\b/i.test(rest)) continue; // has a real DEFAULT/VALUE clause => safe

WARNING: there is a second, DIFFERENT occurrence of the text DEFAULT|VALUE a few lines above, inside a larger regex that extracts the TYPE by looking ahead for clause keywords. That one is correct and must NOT be modified. Only the single-line `if` statement shown above changes.

Why. The exemption is meant to skip a field that supplies its own value through a DEFAULT or VALUE clause. Because the dollar sign is a non-word character, the word boundary in the current pattern also matches inside the standard SurrealDB variable, so a field that merely mentions that variable in an ASSERT or PERMISSIONS clause is wrongly treated as safe and skips the hazard check entirely.

Verified by a one-variable experiment against the real exported function: a plain non-optional field is refused; the same field with an assertion referencing the standard value variable passes; renaming that variable to a shorter name restores the refusal; an assertion that does not mention it is refused; and a genuine VALUE clause is correctly exempt both before and after the change, including the form that assigns from the variable itself. In the migration corpus 56 DEFINE FIELD statements reference that variable, so this is the dominant idiom rather than an edge case.

Change only that one line and no other file.
